rationale: Requires verifying that message content arrives unchanged, which is data integrity.
Identity data and spending history must be kept from anyone but the authorised issuer, which is confidentiality.
Requires continued service while rejecting injection and brute-force floods from hostile clients, which is resistance to attack.
Forces periodic replacement of the sign-in credential before further sign-ins, a credential-based authentication control.
Requires biometric identification of the developer before signing, which is authentication.
Managers must prove identity with a valid credential before the screen is shown, which is authentication.
Hash comparison against the stored archive hash reveals alteration, which is integrity.
Sets a minimum strength for operator credentials, an authentication control, but the text does not state an attack-resistance goal.
Blocks telemetry that would disclose source code against disclosure rules, protecting against unauthorised disclosure.
Idle-session closure explicitly aims to prevent abuse of an abandoned session by an attacker (rule 7).
Obfuscating strings and licence keys so they cannot be read from the binary conceals data from disclosure.
Only users presenting a valid registered identity token may submit jobs, which is identity verification.
Separate read and write permissions limit who can view and who can change each component (rule 3).
Blocks all insert, update and delete by guests, restricting modification; the view access granted is not a restriction on reading.
Requires that passport and payment data were protected against disclosure in transit and discards unprotected data.
Limits patient data exposed to each module to the needed fields, withholding the rest from view.
An integrity mark lets later modification of the binary be detected.
Requires stored data to stay correct and consistent with the statement's intended effect, a data correctness requirement.
Encrypted link protocol prevents interception of content, with no mention of alteration detection.
Signature verification confirms the file originated from an authorised consortium member (origin) and detects alteration, with no non-repudiation claim.
Flags images whose embedded ownership mark was removed or changed, detecting alteration.
Clearing memory with streams and credentials prevents disclosure of leftover content.
Only holders of the editor role may create or change scenarios, restricting modification.
Validates ranges and formats and rejects inconsistent records, ensuring data accuracy and coherence.
Restricts who can change the edit entitlements for forecast datasets, limiting modification rights.
Hash verification discards rule sets that were altered, detecting modification; origin is not mentioned.
Requires an identity confirmation of the owner before the credential can be replaced, which is identity verification.
Detecting reuse of a retired session token is detection of replay, which falls under resistance.
Requires identifying each developer by a distinct credential before accepting jobs, which is authentication.
Requires commands to be executed exactly as specified with matching device state, an accuracy requirement closest to integrity.
Restricts viewing of node addresses and capacity to the administrator role.
A MAC over the history lets the terminal recognise tampering, which is integrity.
Hash comparison rejects datasets that differ from the recorded value, detecting alteration.
Locks the card on detected fault-induction manipulation, a secure state under malicious attack.
Format validation prevents corruption of stored reservations; the text does not state an attacker, so resistance is undecided.
Requires salary values to be recorded exactly with no unintended alteration of stored values.
Reversals are accepted only if source and totals match the original load, protecting loaded data from improper modification; whether source matching is an origin authentication check is unclear.
Verifies the employee's PIN against a stored reference before granting access, which is authentication.
Verifies the analyst's X.509 certificate at sign-in and reuses the verified identity, which is authentication.
